page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz with a dedicated core allocation and one thread per core, this instance features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing both register in the top 25%. However, the ARMv9 architecture exhibits a tradeoff in cryptographic operations, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%. Additionally, while small-model LLM inference is average, prompt processing for a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gd.2xlarge offers balanced resource density by combining dedicated ARMv9 cores with high-speed local NVMe storage. This makes it highly suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from local scratch space. It is less suited for heavy cryptographic processing or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.2xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of RAM, a 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and a baseline network speed of 4 Gbps. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers top-tier memory performance, ranking in the top 10% of Passmark memory benchmarks, alongside strong single-threaded text processing and decompression capabilities. However, it exhibits lower performance in cryptographic tasks and medium-model LLM prompt processing. This resource profile offers balanced qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cores and fast local storage, such as database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose application hosting.
